title: Adaptive Shower Shield
tagline: An assistive device designed with, and for, one specific user.
summary: Through Tikkun Olam Makers, my team developed an adjustable facial shower shield for a child with autism and sensory processing disorder. I designed and iterated the thermoplastic ear guard that made it adjustable and comfortable.

meta.role: Ear guard design and fabrication, symposium presentation

sections.heading: The challenge
sections.body: Our need-knower, a child with autism and sensory processing disorder, found showering distressing because of water on the face. The goal was a facial shower shield that keeps water off the face while staying comfortable enough to actually be worn.

sections.heading: My role
sections.body:
- Designed the ear guard that holds the shield in place, modeled it in SolidWorks, and fabricated it from thermoplastic filament.
- Iterated the ear guard design to make the device adjustable and more comfortable.
- Presented the group's work at a symposium of peers, faculty, and need-knowers.

sections.heading: Design process
sections.body: Because the device had exactly one user, comfort and fit mattered more than anything else. I iterated the ear guard in thermoplastic until it could be adjusted to the user's head, which made the whole device more comfortable to wear.

sections.heading: Results
sections.body: The adjustable thermoplastic ear guard improved user comfort, and both the need-knower and their caregiver gave positive feedback on the final device.
